sections.heading: What the Signs Usually Mean
body: Here's what each sign usually points to.

items.title: A breaker that trips again right after you reset it
items.text: An overloaded circuit, a short or a ground fault. A breaker that's warm or won't reset needs an electrician.

items.title: An outlet or switch plate that's warm or discolored
items.text: A loose connection, which heats up. Stop using it and call us.

items.title: Dead outlets in several rooms
items.text: Often one failed connection upstream, sometimes a breaker. We follow the circuit instead of replacing outlets one by one.

items.title: Lights that flicker in more than one room
items.text: One fixture is usually a bulb. Several rooms points to a loose connection or an overloaded service.

items.title: A garage or outbuilding with no power
items.text: A tripped ground-fault outlet, a bad breaker or a wire that has been cut or pulled loose.

items.title: A buzz, a crackle or a burning smell
items.text: Switch that circuit off and call us. Don't wait for the weekend.

sections.quote: Ben was very good at explaining every diagnostic step and found and corrected the problem, a bad breaker
sections.name: Mark N.

sections.heading: Older Houses and Other People's Wiring
body: Older houses pile up changes: added circuits, spliced wires, a breaker that was never the right size, work done by a previous owner. The wiring doesn't match any drawing.
That's work we take on. We open it up, follow the wire and tell you what's wrong and where it goes from there.

sections.quote: Quick, efficient, and professional. Lost power to my garage and they fixed it up. Pointed out the previous home owners diy mess and pointed out where we go from there.
sections.name: Che J.

sections.heading: Repair, or Something Bigger?
body: Most repairs are small: a breaker, an outlet, a connection. Sometimes the cause is bigger, like an old panel that has no room left or a service that can't carry the house.
When that's the case, we lay out your options and the price of each. You decide.
The cause isn't always where you'd guess. Candice S. blamed her AC for a skyrocketing electric bill, and the problem was a well pump running constantly.

sections.heading: Why We Don't Just Swap the Outlet
body: A new outlet on a bad circuit stops working again. So we test first, find where the power stops and fix that, not the symptom. Mark N. wrote that Ben explained every diagnostic step and found a bad breaker.
It takes a little longer than a swap.

unverified.heading: What we couldn't verify, and why it matters
unverified.intro: We marked these on the demo as yellow "to confirm" tags instead of guessing, because we won't put a claim on your site we can't back up. Your current site says "years of experience" with no number, and shows no license number, warranty or list of towns.

items.why: A homeowner letting someone into an older house wants to know you've been doing this a while, and a made-up number is worse than none.
Someone with a panel or messy wiring wants to look up the license before they let you open the wall.
"Surrounding areas" doesn't tell a homeowner in a town outside Wichita whether you'll come look.
If a repair fails again, the homeowner who already made three calls wants to know you'll stand behind it.

unverified.closing: This is what our onboarding call nails down. Fifteen minutes, and every tag becomes a real, true line.

why: Your site says “With years of experience” and “integrity, expertise, and exceptional customer service,” and it shows the same four reviews on every page. Your Google reviews say something else: Elena W. wrote that Ben came to look at an electrical mess when others wouldn’t, and Wayne R. that other companies wouldn’t address his panel’s safety concerns. Today that sits on Google, not on your site.
On a phone your site is laid out almost twice as wide as the screen, and the phone number isn’t a tap-to-call link. The Lighting card on your homepage goes back to the homepage.
So the demo tells one story: the electrician who comes to look at the hard ones. It opens with electrician in Wichita, KS, and gives electrical repair and lighting installation a page each.
